chunk-001:c001.proposition: Contingent things cannot receive their ultimate explanation from another contingent thing or from the whole collection of contingent things, so contingent reality requires an explanation beyond the universe.

orphanFallback.rationale: Horn presents this as an independent positive inference: contingent reality calls for a reason for its existence, and another contingent member cannot provide the ultimate explanatory terminus.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Because derivative actualizers cannot explain the actuality of the entire series, change requires a first actualizer that is pure actuality and is not itself actualized.

orphanFallback.rationale: The act-and-potency reasoning is offered as a freestanding route from observed change to a purely actual cause, using the locomotive analogy to distinguish derivative from underived actualization.

chunk-001:c005.proposition: A purely actual first cause must be changeless, timeless, immaterial, unlimited in power, and necessarily existent rather than a changing material constituent of the universe.

orphanFallback.rationale: Horn directly derives these attributes from pure actuality, transcendence of space and time, unrestricted actuality, and independence, so the proposition independently advances divine identification.

chunk-001:c006.proposition: The universe's cause is personal and all-knowing because abstract entities lack causal efficacy, creation from nothing calls for agent explanation, and necessary truths require a necessarily existing mind.

orphanFallback.rationale: The source supplies a positive identification argument from causal agency and the grounding of necessary truths to a necessary, unlimited mind, without depending on an opposing move.

chunk-001:c007.proposition: Objective moral facts support God's existence because discovered moral truths require an objective foundation, and the first cause is supremely good as their divine source.

orphanFallback.rationale: Apart from its engagement with a well-being account, the candidate explicitly states a positive moral argument—moral realism is true and, if true, supports God—and connects objective morality to divine goodness.

chunk-002:c002-03.proposition: Quantum randomness does not refute sufficient reason because quantum events can have probabilistic causes, exhibit experimentally usable regularity, and admit interpretations with deterministic hidden causes.

orphanFallback.rationale: The underlying distinction is independently constructive: probabilistic causation is still causation, and stable experimental regularities provide explanatory structure even without a uniquely determined outcome.

chunk-002:c002-05.proposition: Human persons can originate rational choices, and the reality of moral responsibility supports free will even if its mechanism is not yet completely explained.

orphanFallback.rationale: The candidate contains a freestanding affirmative case for agency: persons can cause rational actions, incomplete mechanism does not entail nonexistence, and ordinary moral responsibility supplies positive reason to affirm freedom.

chunk-002:c002-06.proposition: God may permit pain, death, and other privations within a finite physical order when they enable greater goods or prevent greater evils, so natural suffering need not be gratuitous.

orphanFallback.rationale: Horn positively characterizes natural evils as privations within finite systems and identifies animal functioning, virtue, greater goods, and prevention of worse evils as possible justifying roles.

chunk-002:c002-07.proposition: Animal life can remain worth having despite substantial pain, so permitting animals to continue existing need not be incompatible with divine goodness merely because their lives include suffering.

orphanFallback.rationale: The animal-only Earth thought experiment independently supports the proposition that a life containing suffering may still possess sufficient value to make continued animal existence preferable to its elimination.

chunk-002:c002-09.proposition: A limited principle requiring reasons for why things exist, rather than determining explanations for every event, survives quantum indeterminacy and still supports the inference from contingent reality to a necessary being.

orphanFallback.rationale: Horn expressly formulates an existence-focused PSR and maintains that it supports the contingency inference even if some particular events lack determinate explanations, making the distinction independently usable.
